step: Confirm E-7 occupational sub-code, salary floor, and points-based eligibility before drafting offer
field_label: Occupational sub-code; education level; years of relevant experience; proposed salary vs Korean average wage; TOPIK score
deadline_label: At least 3 months before intended entry — before issuing employment offer
non_obvious_official_guidance: E-7 (Specially Designated Activities) visa applicants are assessed under a points-based system. Key criteria are education level, relevant work experience, proposed salary relative to the Korean industry average for the occupation, and Korean language proficiency (TOPIK).
non_obvious_actual_reality: Many employers discover only at the CVIN filing stage that the proposed salary falls below the immigration authority's occupational minimum — a common outright rejection reason. The E-7 category contains dozens of occupational sub-codes; filing under the wrong code changes the required documents and causes delays or rejection. A candidate near the threshold can push over it with a TOPIK language score.
non_obvious_action_required: Identify the precise E-7 occupational sub-code and its salary floor before issuing the offer letter. Verify the applicant's points total against the current published threshold. Ensure the employment contract salary matches the offer letter exactly — discrepancies cause CVIN rejection.
source: Korea Immigration Service — E-7 Visa Guide

step: Employer applies for Confirmation of Visa Issuance Number (사증발급인정서 / CVIN)
form_name: 사증발급인정서 신청서 (Application for Confirmation of Visa Issuance)
field_label: Confirmation of Visa Issuance Number (CVIN)
deadline_label: At least 6–8 weeks before employee's intended entry date
non_obvious_official_guidance: The employer must file a visa issuance certificate petition with the competent Korea Immigration Service regional office on behalf of the foreign national. Only after approval can the employee apply for a visa stamp at a Korean consulate abroad.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Many employers assume the employee can simply apply directly at a Korean consulate abroad, as in most other countries. In Korea the CVIN is a domestic employer-led step that must precede any consular application — without it the employee cannot obtain a work visa stamp. Approval takes 2–4 weeks but can stretch longer at peak periods; missing or uncertified documents cause outright rejection requiring a full re-application.
non_obvious_action_required: Gather before filing: business registration certificate, signed employment contract, company financial statements (3 years), and employee's degree certificates with apostille or consular notarisation plus certified Korean translation. Submit at the competent regional immigration office or via the HiKorea employer portal. Do not book flights until CVIN is confirmed in hand.
source: Korea Immigration Service — Visa Issuance Certificate

step: Employee applies for work visa stamp (E-7 or relevant E-type) at Korean consulate using CVIN
authority: Korean Embassy or Consulate in country of residence
field_label: Visa type code; CVIN number; passport with at least 6 months validity; passport photo
deadline_label: After CVIN received — at least 2–3 weeks before intended entry
source: Korea e-Visa Portal

step: Obtain apostilled criminal record check and medical certificate for E-2 visa application
authority: Korean consulate in country of residence; home-country police authority
field_label: Apostilled criminal record from home country; medical fitness certificate from approved institution
deadline_label: Allow 4–6 weeks for apostille — complete before consular appointment
non_obvious_official_guidance: E-2 visa applicants must submit an apostilled criminal background check issued by their home-country authority and a medical certificate. Requirements are set by the Korean consulate in the applicant's country of residence.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Apostilled criminal record checks from countries such as the US, Canada, and Australia take 4–6 weeks to obtain. Requirements differ by nationality and consulate — the list published on an individual consulate's website supersedes any generic guide. Some consulates additionally require documents to be notarised by the Korean consulate before submission.
non_obvious_action_required: Start the criminal record apostille process at least 6 weeks before the intended consular appointment. Check the specific Korean consulate website for your country — do not rely on generic lists. Confirm whether additional Korean consular notarisation of documents is required.
source: Korea e-Visa Portal — E-2 Visa Requirements

step: Apply for F-3 dependent visa for accompanying spouse and minor children
authority: Korean Embassy or Consulate in country of residence
field_label: Primary visa holder visa type and number; apostilled marriage certificate; apostilled birth certificates; certified Korean translations
deadline_label: Concurrently with or after the primary work visa application
non_obvious_official_guidance: Spouses and minor children of E-1 through E-7 visa holders are eligible for the F-3 (Dependent Family) visa, which permits residence in Korea but not employment.
non_obvious_actual_reality: F-3 holders cannot work legally in Korea. A dependent spouse who wishes to work must separately apply for an independent work visa (such as E-7 or D-10 job-seeker) from within Korea. All foreign civil documents (marriage certificate, birth certificates) must be apostilled and accompanied by certified Korean translations; some consulates additionally require Korean consular notarisation, which adds significant lead time.
non_obvious_action_required: Prepare apostilled marriage certificate and birth certificates for each child. Obtain certified Korean translations from a sworn translator. Confirm with the specific Korean consulate whether additional Korean consular notarisation steps are needed. Plan for the F-3 approval to potentially lag behind the primary work visa approval.
source: Korea Immigration Service — F-3 Dependent Visa

step: Complete mandatory in-Korea medical examination required before ARC issuance for E-2 holders
authority: Korea Immigration Service; immigration-designated medical institutions
field_label: Drug screening result; communicable disease screening result; name of designated medical facility
deadline_label: Before Alien Registration Card is issued — complete within first 30 days
non_obvious_official_guidance: E-2 (foreign language instructor) visa holders must undergo a medical examination at an immigration-designated institution in Korea. Results are submitted as part of the Alien Registration Card application.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The exam tests for illegal drugs and communicable diseases. A positive drug result leads to deportation and visa cancellation. Some medications that are legal abroad are controlled substances in Korea — employees taking prescription ADHD medications, opioids, or certain sedatives should consult an immigration attorney before travel, as the prescription defence does not automatically prevent a positive immigration outcome.
non_obvious_action_required: Book the in-Korea medical exam at an immigration-designated facility immediately upon arrival — results take 1–2 weeks and the ARC cannot be issued without them. Bring full documentation of any prescription medications. Do not assume a home-country prescription exempts you from Korean controlled-substance rules.
source: Korea Immigration Service — E-2 Medical Examination Requirement

step: Open a Korean bank account for salary receipt
authority: Commercial bank (KB Kookmin, Shinhan, KEB Hana, Woori, IBK)
field_label: Passport with valid visa; employer certificate (재직증명서); proof of address; ARC if already issued
deadline_label: Within first week of arrival for interim account — upgrade to full account once ARC is issued
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign nationals may open bank accounts in Korea using their passport and visa. Full-featured accounts with internet banking and transfer functions generally require the Alien Registration Card.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Without an ARC, most banks open only a restricted foreigner account with no internet banking and low transfer limits. Attempting to open an account at a standard branch without a dedicated foreigner-services desk typically results in refusal. Certain major banks (Shinhan Bank, KEB Hana Bank) operate foreigner-dedicated branches or counters in Seoul (Itaewon, Gangnam, Yeouido) with English-speaking staff that can process interim accounts.
non_obvious_action_required: Identify a foreigner-friendly branch in advance — call ahead to confirm English-language service. Bring: passport, visa, employer certificate (재직증명서 from HR), and proof of address. Return to the same branch to upgrade the account to a full account once the ARC is issued.
source: Financial Supervisory Service Korea — Foreign Residents

step: Report move-in address at local community service centre (주민센터)
field_label: Korean residential address; lease agreement or accommodation proof; ARC (or passport if ARC not yet issued)
deadline_label: Within 14 days of moving into accommodation
non_obvious_official_guidance: All residents in Korea must report a change of address (전입신고) to the local community service centre (주민센터) within 14 days of moving in. Foreign nationals with an ARC must include their ARC number.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Foreigners technically need an ARC to complete the formal 전입신고 with their ARC number, but establishing proof of address is itself a prerequisite for many tasks (bank account, NHIS, tax). In practice, most new arrivals use a signed lease agreement (월세/전세 계약서) as interim proof of address for other tasks and complete the formal 전입신고 at the 주민센터 once the ARC is issued.
non_obvious_action_required: Secure a signed lease or employer accommodation letter immediately upon arrival to use as interim address proof for HR and banking. Complete the formal 전입신고 at the nearest 주민센터 as soon as the ARC is in hand. Bring: ARC, lease agreement, and the landlord's ID or building register (등기부등본).
source: HiKorea — Address Registration for Foreigners

step: Apply for Alien Registration Card (외국인등록증 / ARC) at regional immigration office or online via HiKorea
authority: Korea Immigration Service — Regional Immigration Office
field_label: ARC number (issued on registration); passport; valid visa; Korean address proof; passport photo 3.5×4.5 cm; employer certificate
deadline_label: Within 90 days of entry date
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign nationals intending to stay in Korea for more than 90 days must apply for an Alien Registration Card at a Korea Immigration Service regional office within 90 days of entry.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Online applications are available via HiKorea (hikorea.go.kr) for many visa categories, avoiding very long in-person queues at busy offices such as Seoul Gangseo, Suwon, and Incheon. The ARC takes 2–3 weeks to be issued after application; a receipt (외국인등록 사실증명) is issued on the application day and functions as interim ID for most purposes. Apply as early as possible after a fixed Korean address is established — appointment slots at major offices can be weeks out.
non_obvious_action_required: Book an appointment via HiKorea before visiting the immigration office. Apply as soon as a permanent Korean address is established — do not wait until day 85–90. Collect the physical ARC in person from the office or designate a representative with a notarised power of attorney.
source: HiKorea — Alien Registration

step: Employer enrols employee in National Health Insurance (건강보험 / NHIS) as workplace subscriber
form_name: 직장가입자 자격취득신고서 (Notification of Acquisition of Workplace Subscriber Qualification)
field_label: ARC number; employer code; employment start date; standard monthly income (보수월액)
deadline_label: Employer must notify NHIS within 14 days of employment start date
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers must enrol foreign employees holding work visas (E-1 through E-7 and others) in the National Health Insurance scheme as workplace subscribers within 14 days of the employment start date.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Since 2019 NHIS participation has been mandatory for most foreigners staying over 6 months. The 2024 combined contribution rate is approximately 7.09% of standard monthly income, split equally: employee ~3.545% + employer ~3.545%. A long-term care insurance (장기요양보험) surcharge of approximately 12.95% of the health insurance premium is added on top. Eligible dependants (spouse, minor children, parents meeting income and asset tests) can be enrolled as co-insured (피부양자) at no additional premium.
non_obvious_action_required: HR must register the employee in the NHIS employer EDI portal or at a local NHIS branch within 14 days of the start date. The employee should confirm enrolment has occurred and request the NHIS membership card (건강보험증). Add eligible dependants as co-insured immediately after their ARC is issued.
source: National Health Insurance Service — Foreigner Enrolment

step: Enrol in National Pension Scheme (국민연금 / NPS) or obtain totalization-agreement exemption
form_name: 사업장가입자 자격취득 신고서 (Notification of Workplace Subscriber Acquisition); 적용 제외 신청서 (Exemption Application) if totalization agreement applies
field_label: ARC number; employer business registration number; standard monthly income; employee nationality for treaty check
deadline_label: Employer enrols within the month employment commences; file exemption application as soon as Certificate of Coverage is obtained from home-country authority
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign workers on qualifying work visas are subject to Korean National Pension contributions (employer 4.5% + employee 4.5% of standard monthly income) unless they are nationals of a country that has a bilateral totalization agreement with Korea and hold a Certificate of Coverage.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Korea has totalization agreements with more than 30 countries including the US, UK, Germany, France, Canada, Australia, Japan, China, and India. Nationals of these countries who hold a Certificate of Coverage from their home-country pension authority (e.g. SSA in the US, HMRC in the UK) can apply to NPS to be exempted from Korean contributions. If the exemption form is not filed, deductions begin automatically and obtaining a retroactive refund is cumbersome. Nationals of non-agreement countries accumulate Korean pension credits and may claim a lump-sum refund of contributions on departure.
non_obvious_action_required: Immediately check whether the employee's home country has a totalization agreement with Korea at nps.or.kr. If yes: obtain the Certificate of Coverage from the home-country authority and file the NPS exemption application before payroll is run. If no: confirm that contributions will apply and keep all NPS contribution statements for a potential departure refund.
source: National Pension Service — International Social Security Agreements

step: Register on Hometax (홈택스) using ARC number as Korean taxpayer ID
field_label: ARC number (serves as Korean taxpayer identification number); Hometax login credential
deadline_label: As soon as ARC is issued
source: National Tax Service — Hometax Portal

step: Elect 19% flat-rate income tax option for foreign workers during year-end settlement
form_name: 외국인 단일세율 적용신청서 (Application for Single Tax Rate for Foreign Employees)
field_label: Election of flat rate vs progressive rate; first calendar year of Korean employment; annual employment income
deadline_label: Elected during 연말정산 (yeonmaljeongsan) — January 15 to February 28 of the following year; irrevocable for that year
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign workers may elect to have Korean employment income taxed at a flat 19% income tax rate (plus 1.9% local income tax = 20.9% total) instead of the progressive rates of 6%–45%, for a maximum of 20 consecutive years of Korean employment.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The flat rate is advantageous for employees earning above approximately KRW 60–70 million gross per year; below that level the progressive system with Korean deductions (credit-card spending, insurance premiums, housing loan interest) is often more favourable. The election is irrevocable once made for a given tax year. The 20-year eligibility clock starts from the first calendar year of Korean employment, not from the year the election is first made — so it cannot be deferred to save years.
non_obvious_action_required: Before January each year, ask the employer's payroll team to model both the flat-rate and progressive-rate outcomes using projected annual income and available deductions. File the election via Hometax or through employer payroll during the 연말정산 period. Engage a Korean tax professional in the first year to make the correct choice.
source: National Tax Service — Foreign Worker Tax Guide

step: Complete year-end tax settlement (연말정산 / yeonmaljeongsan) through employer each January–February
authority: National Tax Service (NTS / 국세청) — processed via employer payroll
form_name: 근로소득 원천징수영수증 (Withholding Tax Receipt for Employment Income)
field_label: Annual employment income; eligible deductions (insurance, housing, credit-card spending, education, medical); resulting refund or additional tax due
deadline_label: Employee submits deduction documents to employer HR by mid-January; employer completes and files by end of February
non_obvious_official_guidance: Korean employers are legally required to conduct an annual year-end tax settlement (연말정산) for all employees, reconciling actual annual income tax liability against monthly withholding amounts.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Foreign workers in their first year often qualify for very few Korean deductions — credit-card deductions require spending in Korea on a Korean-issued card, housing loan deductions require a Korean housing finance loan, and insurance deductions require domestic Korean policies. First-year arrivals therefore commonly owe additional tax rather than receiving a refund, even at the same gross salary as a Korean colleague. The NTS simplified service (연말정산 간소화 서비스) pre-populates eligible deductions from January 15 each year.
non_obvious_action_required: Log into Hometax from January 15 to pull the simplified deduction report. Submit all deduction evidence to employer HR before the internal payroll deadline (typically late January). Confirm which deductions are actually available to you as a foreigner in your current year. Any underpaid amount will be collected via the February payslip.
source: National Tax Service — Year-End Tax Settlement

step: Track 183-day presence threshold for Korean tax residency and worldwide income obligations
field_label: Days physically present in Korea in the tax year; applicable Korea–home country tax treaty; nature and amount of foreign-source income
deadline_label: Residency status assessed at December 31 each year; worldwide income obligation triggered upon crossing 183 days
non_obvious_official_guidance: An individual is a Korean tax resident if they have a domicile in Korea or have resided continuously for 183 days or more in the tax year. Korean tax residents are liable to Korean income tax on worldwide income.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Once tax residency is triggered, overseas income (rental income, foreign dividends, self-employment income from another country) becomes reportable in Korea even if already taxed abroad. Korea has double taxation treaties with over 90 countries, but treaty relief must be actively claimed — it is not automatic. An employee may simultaneously qualify as a tax resident in their home country, creating dual residency that requires tie-breaker analysis under the relevant treaty and potentially additional filing obligations in both jurisdictions.
non_obvious_action_required: Keep a precise day-count record from day one in Korea. If you have material overseas income, engage a Korean tax advisor before the 183-day mark is crossed to assess treaty position and foreign-income reporting obligations. Review the Korea–[home country] tax treaty's tie-breaker and dividend/rental articles before filing.
source: National Tax Service — Resident vs Non-Resident Taxation

step: Assess and document permanent establishment (PE) risk from employee's Korea-based activities
field_label: Nature of employee's authority in Korea (contract negotiation, signing, client management); duration; fixed office or home-office location
deadline_label: Ongoing from first day of Korea-based employment
non_obvious_official_guidance: A foreign enterprise may create a taxable permanent establishment in Korea if an employee habitually exercises authority to conclude contracts in Korea on behalf of the enterprise, or if it maintains a fixed place of business — including a home office used regularly — in Korea.
non_obvious_actual_reality: PE risk is systematically underestimated by foreign companies that place their first Korea-based employee without a Korean legal entity. NTS audits increasingly target foreign companies with Korea-based staff acting as dependent agents, and a finding of PE triggers Korean corporate income tax on all Korea-attributable profits retrospectively — not just on employment costs. Transfer pricing obligations also apply to internal charges between the foreign head office and the Korean activities even below the formal PE threshold.
non_obvious_action_required: Before the employee starts work in Korea, instruct the company's international tax advisors to assess PE exposure under the Korea–[home country] income tax treaty. Define the employee's role in writing to remain within auxiliary or preparatory functions if no Korean entity exists. Maintain contemporaneous records of the employee's actual daily activities and client interactions.
source: National Tax Service — International Tax / PE

step: Report any employer or workplace change to Korea Immigration Service within 15 days
form_name: 근무처 변경·추가 신고서 (Report of Change or Addition of Workplace)
field_label: New employer name; new employer business registration number; ARC number; effective date of change
deadline_label: Within 15 days of the change of employer or workplace (Immigration Act Article 21)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign nationals on E-category work visas must report any change or addition of employer to the Korea Immigration Service within 15 days of the change under the Immigration Act.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Failure to report — including an intra-group transfer to a different Korean legal entity — constitutes a status violation that can result in immigration penalties and jeopardise visa renewal. Additionally, some changes involve a shift in occupational category that requires a full visa change application rather than a simple report; filing only a report in that scenario is legally insufficient and the employee will be in unauthorised status for the new role.
non_obvious_action_required: Any time the employer, legal entity, or principal workplace changes, file a workplace change report via HiKorea or the nearest immigration office within 15 days. If the new role represents a change in occupational category (e.g. from engineering to sales management), seek immigration advice before the move — a visa change application may need to be approved before the new role commences.
source: Korea Immigration Service — Workplace Change Notification

step: Renew visa stay permission and Alien Registration Card before expiry
form_name: 체류기간 연장허가 신청서 (Application for Extension of Stay Period); 외국인등록증 재발급 신청서 (ARC Re-issue Application)
field_label: ARC expiry date; renewed employment contract or extension letter; updated company financials; passport with remaining validity
deadline_label: Apply at least 2 months before ARC and visa expiry — appointment slots at major offices can be weeks out
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign nationals must extend their visa stay permission and renew their ARC before the expiry date. ARC expiry is the same date as the visa stay permission expiry.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Overstaying by even one day incurs an immediate fine and can bar the employee from future Korean visa issuance for up to 5 years. Popular immigration offices (Seoul Gangseo, Suwon, Incheon) have very long appointment backlogs — begin the renewal process 2–3 months before expiry. Employer must provide an updated employment contract, salary certificate, and recent company financial statements for the renewal application.
non_obvious_action_required: Set a calendar reminder 3 months before expiry. Confirm with employer that a renewal employment letter and updated financials are prepared. Book a HiKorea appointment early. Verify that passport validity extends at least 6 months beyond the requested new visa end date before attending the appointment.
source: HiKorea — Visa Extension and ARC Renewal

step: Report change of residential address to Korea Immigration Service within 14 days of every move
form_name: 외국인 체류지 변경신고서 (Report of Change of Foreigner's Place of Residence)
field_label: New Korean address; ARC number; new lease agreement or accommodation proof
deadline_label: Within 14 days of moving to a new address
non_obvious_official_guidance: ARC holders must notify the Korea Immigration Service of any change in their residential address within 14 days of the change. The update can be filed online via HiKorea for most ARC holders.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Many foreigners are aware of the 전입신고 (move-in report at the local 주민센터) but are unaware that a separate immigration address notification is also mandatory. Failure to update the immigration record creates administrative problems at ARC renewal and visa applications. Both the district office notification and the immigration address update must be completed — one does not satisfy the other.
non_obvious_action_required: On any move, file both: (1) 전입신고 at the local 주민센터 and (2) immigration address change via HiKorea or the nearest immigration office — both within 14 days. Keep a copy of the new lease agreement as supporting evidence for both filings.
source: HiKorea — Change of Residence Address

step: Claim lump-sum refund of NPS contributions on permanent departure (nationals of non-totalization-agreement countries)
form_name: 반환일시금 지급청구서 (Claim for Lump-Sum Refund of Pension Contributions)
field_label: Total NPS contributions paid; departure date; Korean bank account or overseas remittance details for refund
deadline_label: Claim within 5 years of permanent departure from Korea
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign nationals from countries without a bilateral totalization agreement with Korea who have paid NPS contributions but do not meet the minimum eligibility period for a Korean pension may claim a lump-sum refund of all contributions plus accrued interest upon departure.
non_obvious_actual_reality: A significant number of departing foreign workers fail to claim this refund and forfeit it after the 5-year limitation period expires. For nationals of totalization-agreement countries, Korean contribution credits are transferred to the home-country pension system — a separate Korean lump-sum refund is generally not available in that case. Clarifying treaty status before departure is therefore essential, as the two outcomes are mutually exclusive and the wrong assumption causes either a lost refund or a failed credit transfer.
non_obvious_action_required: Before leaving Korea permanently: confirm your country's totalization agreement status with Korea at nps.or.kr. If no agreement: file the lump-sum refund claim at any NPS branch or via the NPS website before departure or within 5 years after. If a totalization agreement applies: contact your home-country pension authority to initiate the credit transfer process. Keep all NPS contribution statements throughout employment.
source: National Pension Service — Lump-Sum Refund for Departing Foreigners
